   ```
author: risingorange
body:
When the central error handler catches an `AnkiHubHTTPError` with a status code of 403, it tries to get the `detail` field of the json content from the response. However the code currently does not handle the case when the response doesn't contain json content and raises a `JSONDecodeError` in this situation. 

The consequence is that both errors, `AnkiHubHTTPError` and `JSONDecodeError` are sent to Sentry. An error dialog about the `AnkiHubHTTPError` is shown to the user. 
The intended consequences would be that only the `AnkiHubHTTPError` is sent to Sentry and shown to the user.

## Related issues
[fix: JSONDecodeError in exception handler](https://www.notion.so/ankihub/AnkiHub-Planning-7d2bdb8e15034c559bef129adbe163b7?p=dd4844eeb6dc4bb89e884b0ef6ac6741&pm=c)

https://ankihub.sentry.io/issues/4407875330/?project=6546414&query=exception+handler+threw&referrer=issue-stream&sort=freq&statsPeriod=90d&stream_index=4


## Proposed changes
- Catch the `JSONDecodeError` and return `False` in `_maybe_handle_ankihub_http_error`. Then `_try_handle_exception` will return `False` as well, `handled` will be `False` and the error will be passed to `_maybe_report_exception_and_show_feedback_dialog` here:
https://github.com/ankipalace/ankihub_addon/blob/f46515a516b3e54ecbd644b1ad2db7733504a312/ankihub/gui/errors.py#L191-L207
- Add test and refactor other tests in `TestErrorHandling`

author: risingorange
body:
Users sometimes get an `AnkiHubHTTPError` with status code 401 when syncing with AnkiWeb and AnkiHub. (It should be handled by the exception handler, but there is an exception in the exception handler.) 
A large part of these exceptions is caused by  `ankihub.gui.auto_sync.sync_with_ankiweb` getting called twice and then causing this error: `DbError { info: "SqliteFailure(Error { code: Unknown, extended_code: 1 }, Some(\"cannot start a transaction within a transaction\"))", kind: Other }`. The flow is quite complicated. (See [this event](https://ankihub.sentry.io/issues/4649135864/?project=6546414&query=exception+handler+threw&referrer=issue-stream&sort=freq&statsPeriod=90d&stream_index=1) on Sentry. You can see from the logs in the breadcrumbs section that `mw._sync_collection_and_media` is called twice and then the `DBError` happens.)
The `DBError` (which is raised when `taskman._on_closures_pending` is called) is causing the exception handler to fail at handling the `AnkiHubHTTPError`. 

The intended behavior would be for the exception handler to catch the 401 and open the login dialog.

## Related issues
[fix: AnkiHubHTTPError with status code 401 not getting handled](https://www.notion.so/ankihub/AnkiHub-Planning-7d2bdb8e15034c559bef129adbe163b7?p=afec657a4f9041f58d81dd8d0a100746&pm=c)

Sentry: https://ankihub.sentry.io/issues/4649135864/?project=6546414&query=exception+handler+threw&referrer=issue-stream&sort=freq&statsPeriod=90d&stream_index=1

Some forum posts (there are more):
https://community.ankihub.net/t/anki-failing-to-sync/121331/3
https://community.ankihub.net/t/report-error-unknown-how-to-fix/95411

## Proposed changes
- Prevent `ankihub.gui.operations.ankihub_sync.sync_with_ankihub` from raising exceptions when they occur within the function.
 The purpose of this is to prevent `sync_with_ankiweb` getting called twice here, because that causes the `DBError`:
  https://github.com/ankipalace/ankihub_addon/blob/e05783297e1590e71289503fb28aa83de428a284/ankihub/gui/auto_sync.py#L87-L91
  `_maybe_sync_with_ankihub` calls `sync_with_ankihub`. Currently, when there is an exception in `sync_with_ankihub`, `sync_with_ankiweb` will be called twice: once as a callback by `sync_with_ankihub` and once at line 91 in the code above.
 
   The `sync_with_ankihub` operations takes an `on_done` callback and follows a pattern where any exceptions that occur during the operation are passed to the `on_done` callback. 
  We don't want exceptions which happen in `sync_with_ankihub` to be back-propagated to the code that calls it.
  
  This can be achieved by using `aqt.mw.taskman.run_on_main`:
  https://github.com/ankipalace/ankihub_addon/blob/e05783297e1590e71289503fb28aa83de428a284/ankihub/gui/operations/ankihub_sync.py#L77-L80

  The mechanism by which the back-propagation is stopped are PyQt signals and slots. `run_on_main` triggers the function which is passed to it by calling `emit()` on a signal. PyQt. doesn't back-propagate exceptions through `emit()` calls.
- Add tests
  
## How to reproduce
- Run the added tests to see that exceptions which happen in `sync_with_ankihub` are not back-propagated to the calling code
- To reproduce the exception handler opening the login dialog when an 401 response occurs, you can do this:
  - Login to AnkiWeb in Anki (you need an AnkiWeb accounts for this)
  - Close Anki
  - Find the folder for the add-on data related to your current Anki profile in the `ankihub_base` folder at the root of the repo
  - Change the token value in the `.private_config.json` file to an invalid token
  - Start Anki
  - Anki will automatically try to sync with AnkiHub and sync with AnkiWeb
  - The AnkiHub login dialog will open
 
Here's a video of the login dialog showing up when starting Anki after changing the token:  

https://github.com/ankipalace/ankihub_addon/assets/31575114/8abb0cd0-d75d-4b0d-9a41-79ebda45239e

Note that the login dialog might appear behind the Anki window.

#### Description Of Changes
This addresses some limitations in `isentropic_interpolation` and `isentropic_interpolation_as_dataset` identified in #3315, which is trying to use the functionality on WRF output natively on a sigma vertical coordinate.

* Don't blindly assume that the vertical coordinate is pressure in `isentropic_interpolation_as_dataset` but check the dimensionality and issue a more useful `ValueError`
* Tweak the handling of pressure in `isentropic_interpolation` to work with a *passed-in* 3D pressure field, since internally we were already using a 3D pressure field
* Allow `isentropic_interpolation_as_dataset` to work with data on non-pressure coordinates by accepting a `pressure` kw-only argument in this case, which overrides using the vertical coordinate.

## What changes does this PR introduce?
No "real" changes but a cleaner code without duplicated calls to ECCO_CHECK (from `ecco_cost_init_fixed.F` and from the standard place in `packages_check.F`).

## What is the current behaviour? 
ECCO_CHECK is called 2 times, see above. Note that, in addition to checking `pkg/ecco`, it also checks for many files and turns off some `pkg/ecco` switches. For this reason, it seems better to call `ECCO_SUMMARY` only after these checks.

## What is the new behaviour 
Comment out calls to ECCO_CHECK and ECCO_SUMMARY in `ecco_cost_init_fixed.F`  and only keep the call to ECCO_CHECK from  `packages_check.F`, with ECCO_SUMMARY now being called at the end of `ecco_check.F`

## Does this PR introduce a breaking change? 
No

## Other information:
Also, in `packages_check.F`,  move call to ECCO_CHECK before GRDCHK_CHECK to get ECCO summary before grdchk summary.

## Suggested addition to `tag-index`
o pkg/ecco:

    call from packages_check.F) and move ECCO_SUMMARY call to ecco_check.F

author: deploy-code-org
body:
# I18n Sync Down & Out

This PR contains all changes to translations made since the last sync (usually a week).

## To Review:

Look through the changes in each of the commits and verify that all changes are expected. Note that **it is not necessary to review every single "dashboard i18n update" commit.** These commits are batched by language to make it easier to review just a couple commits in this category.

### Things to Note:

- We expect translation changes to come in on a regular basis; new strings will be translated, existing translations will be updated, and source string removals will result in translations for those strings also being removed.

- We expect translations to arrive in large batches, so don't worry if you see a large group of changes in a specific language.

- We _do not_ usually expect to see a large number of formatting changes, or batches of changes that apply to strings in every single language. If you see this, it usually means either that a code change went in or that something broke.

## Known Issues:

- If the CI unit tests fail at the `grunt messages:all` step, they will typically fail with a message like:

  ```
  [2019-10-04 02:38:57] Running "messages:all" (messages) task
  [2019-10-04 02:39:00] Warning: Error processing localization file i18n/common/zh_tw.json: SyntaxError: Expected [0-9a-zA-Z$_] but "\u8A0A" found. Use --force to continue. 
  ```

  This usually means that a translator has translated one of the [MessageFormat variables](https://messageformat.github.io/messageformat/guide/#variables). In this case, you should find and fix the offending translation in crowdin, and then manually update the associated strings in `i18n/locales` and `apps/i18n`.

  See https://github.com/code-dot-org/code-dot-org/pull/31098/commits/ab3e5d1d740869a880f2e9da5cf0a4348886915e and https://github.com/code-dot-org/code-dot-org/pull/31098/commits/0fca37658cacaaff55d9adfc9d04c40b37cc5e2d for an example.

## To Deploy:

Once one or two people have reviewed and approved this change and the tests are passing, ship it!

It's not necessary to wait for everyone on the team to review.

<details>
  <summary>Changelog</summary>
  
  
   ### 7.3.3
   ```
   --------------------------

- Fix: function definitions with multi-line signatures can now be excluded by
  matching any of the lines, closing `issue 684`_.  Thanks, `Jan Rusak,
  Maciej Kowalczyk and Joanna Ejzel <pull 1705_>`_.

- Fix: XML reports could fail with a TypeError if files had numeric components
  that were duplicates except for leading zeroes, like ``file1.py`` and
  ``file001.py``.  Fixes `issue 1709`_.

- The ``coverage annotate`` command used to announce that it would be removed
  in a future version. Enough people got in touch to say that they use it, so
  it will stay.  Don't expect it to keep up with other new features though.

- Added new :ref:`debug options <cmd_run_debug>`:

  - ``pytest`` writes the pytest test name into the debug output.

  - ``dataop2`` writes the full data being added to CoverageData objects.

.. _issue 684: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/684
.. _pull 1705: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/pull/1705
.. _issue 1709: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1709


.. _changes_7-3-2:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.3.2
   ```
   --------------------------

- The ``coverage lcov`` command ignored the ``[report] exclude_lines`` and
  ``[report] exclude_also`` settings (`issue 1684`_).  This is now fixed,
  thanks `Jacqueline Lee <pull 1685_>`_.

- Sometimes SQLite will create journal files alongside the coverage.py database
  files.  These are ephemeral, but could be mistakenly included when combining
  data files.  Now they are always ignored, fixing `issue 1605`_. Thanks to
  Brad Smith for suggesting fixes and providing detailed debugging.

- On Python 3.12+, we now disable SQLite writing journal files, which should be
  a little faster.

- The new 3.12 soft keyword ``type`` is properly bolded in HTML reports.

- Removed the "fullcoverage" feature used by CPython to measure the coverage of
  early-imported standard library modules.  CPython `stopped using it
  <88054_>`_ in 2021, and it stopped working completely in Python 3.13.

.. _issue 1605: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1605
.. _issue 1684: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1684
.. _pull 1685: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/pull/1685
.. _88054: https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/88054


.. _changes_7-3-1:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.3.1
   ```
   --------------------------

- The semantics of stars in file patterns has been clarified in the docs.  A
  leading or trailing star matches any number of path components, like a double
  star would.  This is different than the behavior of a star in the middle of a
  pattern.  This discrepancy was `identified by Sviatoslav Sydorenko
  <starbad_>`_, who `provided patient detailed diagnosis <pull 1650_>`_ and
  graciously agreed to a pragmatic resolution.

- The API docs were missing from the last version. They are now `restored
  <apidocs_>`_.

.. _apidocs: https://coverage.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api_coverage.html
.. _starbad: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1407#issuecomment-1631085209

   ```
   ### 7.3.0
   ```
   --------------------------

- Added a :meth:`.Coverage.collect` context manager to start and stop coverage
  data collection.

- Dropped support for Python 3.7.

- Fix: in unusual circumstances, SQLite cannot be set to asynchronous mode.
  Coverage.py would fail with the error ``Safety level may not be changed
  inside a transaction.`` This is now avoided, closing `issue 1646`_.  Thanks
  to Michael Bell for the detailed bug report.

  different syntaxes: .coveragerc, pyproject.toml, setup.cfg, and tox.ini.

- Fix: added ``nosemgrep`` comments to our JavaScript code so that
  semgrep-based SAST security checks won't raise false alarms about security
  problems that aren't problems.

--continue-on-cu-index-overflow: missing argument. Changed it so that it is the
same behavior as other flags like -gsplit-dwarf. Where
--continue-on-cu-index-overflow will default to continue, and user can set mode
with --continue-on-cu-index-overflow=\<value>.

author: amlattanzi
body:
This PR is a part of the greater effort to overhaul the moisture classes and how they interact with ERF. The new paradigm is summarized as follows

1. **Microphysics** will own a vector (nlev) that contains pointers to the micro class being used, which is the same at each level.
2. The micro class now creates and owns its own data. If ERF wants qmoist variables, it must query the micro class for a pointer and then use that pointer. **The query should only be done when init is called.**
3. The micro class data (Mic_Fab_Vars) persists along all levels but is now updated after each FillPatch and FillPatchIntermediate call (may be excessive).
4. The micro classes are restructured to have the following operations (**Init, Define, Qmoist_Ptr, Copy_State_to_Micro, Copy_Micro_to_State, Update_Micro_Vars, Update_State_Vars**). We may then start up with one call to **Init, Define** and get the pointers with **Qmoist_ptr**. If the state data changes, the **Update_Micro_Vars** can be called, which is a wrapper to internal functions that do necessary operations on the new data (after it's copied into the micro_fab_vars).

**_TODO:_**
1. General clean up, a lot of legacy code from the old `Init' function was left commented out. This was done since that function was cut into separate operations for clarity. Once verified, this code should be deleted.
2. Iterations to split qt -> qv/qc are NOT implemented. New function and scheme is need.
3. Whenever we re-grid we need to make sure we call **micro.Init()** and then get the new **micro.Qmoist_Ptr()**.
4. Assess FillPatchMoistVars, only the qv component was passed to this routine...

author: jdconrad
body:
This change takes the existing 4 retrievers (classic, knn, linear_combination, and rrf) and uses them to manage the 3 major phases (dfs, query, and fetch), though as this prototype exists now, the work is currently only partially done with the dfs phase completed, and the query phase partially completed.

Current Design:

* Retriever code does not replace existing infrastructure at this time. Instead, it builds a separate path re-using what it can for each of the phases. If this design is successful, over time we can move the old internals to use the new retriever path instead, but I am strongly against trying to do this in a first iteration.
* DFS Phase: The retriever tree (through `RetrieverBuilder`) is walked to setup a `SearchSourceBuilder` that has a dfs query based on which retriever is at the root of the tree. This dfs query should contain all of the required term stats necessary for a full search. The retrievers also setup a `SearchSourceBuilder` with all of the required knn queries since a knn retriever works at the coordinator (global) level. The dfs phase will fan out exactly once to all required shards for an index.
* Query Phase: The retriever tree is walked to setup a `SearchSourceBuilder` *per query*. And one additional `SearchSourceBuilder` if track top hits is set or aggregations are specified. Each required shard will be hit *per query*. While this adds some round trip cost, the trade off is that the query phase on the shard needs very little modification. And each `QuerySearchResult` still only applies to a single query. We also get natural concurrency this way without any further modifications per query.
* Query Phase Result Consumer: There is now a specialized version of this called `RetrieverQueryPhaseResultConsumer` that is designed to handle the number of `QuerySearchResult`s that come in from potentially multiple queries. This portion is still in progress.

Up next for this prototype:
* Query Phase Result Consumer: Retrievers needs to manage the merging of both partial reduction of top docs and the final reduction of top docs. Partial reduction of top docs would be per query and the specific retriever for a query can determine the best way to merge them. The final reduction of top docs would finish up any per query merges, and then if a compound retriever is used, have it generate the final top docs.
* Fetch Phase: The `QuerySearchResult`s need to be trimmed back into a single one per shard to collect the necessary fetch phase information to generate the search response's hits. For explain and possibly profiling, the retrievers can be sent to each shard's fetch phase with the necessary information to do this by storing rescore ideas and possibly sorts for the query the retriever is responsible for. A final explain can be done on the coordinator by the retriever tree for compound retrievers when necessary.

   ```
   --------------------------

- Fix: function definitions with multi-line signatures can now be excluded by
  matching any of the lines, closing `issue 684`_.  Thanks, `Jan Rusak,
  Maciej Kowalczyk and Joanna Ejzel <pull 1705_>`_.

- Fix: XML reports could fail with a TypeError if files had numeric components
  that were duplicates except for leading zeroes, like ``file1.py`` and
  ``file001.py``.  Fixes `issue 1709`_.

- The ``coverage annotate`` command used to announce that it would be removed
  in a future version. Enough people got in touch to say that they use it, so
  it will stay.  Don't expect it to keep up with other new features though.

- Added new :ref:`debug options <cmd_run_debug>`:

  - ``pytest`` writes the pytest test name into the debug output.

  - ``dataop2`` writes the full data being added to CoverageData objects.

.. _changes_7-3-2:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.3.2
   ```
   --------------------------

- The ``coverage lcov`` command ignored the ``[report] exclude_lines`` and
  ``[report] exclude_also`` settings (`issue 1684`_).  This is now fixed,
  thanks `Jacqueline Lee <pull 1685_>`_.

- Sometimes SQLite will create journal files alongside the coverage.py database
  files.  These are ephemeral, but could be mistakenly included when combining
  data files.  Now they are always ignored, fixing `issue 1605`_. Thanks to
  Brad Smith for suggesting fixes and providing detailed debugging.

- On Python 3.12+, we now disable SQLite writing journal files, which should be
  a little faster.

- The new 3.12 soft keyword ``type`` is properly bolded in HTML reports.

- Removed the "fullcoverage" feature used by CPython to measure the coverage of
  early-imported standard library modules.  CPython `stopped using it
  <88054_>`_ in 2021, and it stopped working completely in Python 3.13.

.. _issue 1684: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1684
.. _pull 1685: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/pull/1685

   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.3.1
   ```
   --------------------------

  leading or trailing star matches any number of path components, like a double
  star would.  This is different than the behavior of a star in the middle of a
  pattern.  This discrepancy was `identified by Sviatoslav Sydorenko
  <starbad_>`_, who `provided patient detailed diagnosis <pull 1650_>`_ and
  graciously agreed to a pragmatic resolution.

- The API docs were missing from the last version. They are now `restored
   ```

author: vpax
body:
Currently when a `TableVal` is constructed it creates a corresponding `CompHash` (and deletes it when destructed), even though that value is actually static for the associated `TableType`. This PR shifts its construction to the `TableType`, and also does some additional minor compute-it-once-because-it's-static tweaks.

On a good-sized DNS PCAP (500K requests), _hyperfine_ finds this shaves 2% off of execution time.

#### Problem solved by the commit
We now parse the same metricsets and modify events in the same location for edge and client. 

#### How problem was solved, alternative solutions (if any) and why they were rejected
- We now initialize client events using the same functions in aie_profile_util.cpp just like the edge implementation. Moved the modifyEvents function to the util class and fixed an issue where interface tile events were incorrectly modified by default.
- Also fixed issue with the "schema" missing in new aie_control_config files. We now look for the aiecompiler_options field instead. This will need to be modified at a later date
- Metricsets for input and output stalls in interface tiles for AIE1 were using AIE2 events, and thus were invalid. For AIE1 devices, these events have been changed to use AIE1 events.
